title: Turing's Torch AI Weekly — 2026-03-27
summary: This week's AI Weekly covers the most significant developments in artificial intelligence from the past seven days — practical analysis, no hype, for listeners who want to understand what actually changed and why it matters.

title: GPT-5, Gemini 2, and the Model Race: What Actually Changed
summary: A plain-English breakdown of the GPT-5 and Gemini 2 releases — what the benchmarks actually measure, where the models improve in practice, and how to evaluate capability claims without the press-release framing.
key_takeaways: Benchmark scores and real-world performance diverge significantly for complex reasoning tasks.
Both models show genuine improvements in multi-step instruction following.
Context window increases matter more for enterprise users than consumer use cases.

title: AI Regulation in 2025: What Passed, What Failed, What's Next
summary: An honest accounting of AI regulatory progress in 2025 — which frameworks moved forward, which stalled in committee, and what the patchwork of national approaches means for organisations building or deploying AI systems.
key_takeaways: The EU AI Act's high-risk classification system is operational but enforcement capacity remains limited.
US federal AI legislation failed to advance; state-level frameworks are filling the gap unevenly.
Sector-specific guidance (healthcare, finance) is proving more actionable than general AI regulation.
